title: First Shift: Initial Contact
onScreenMessage: To perform at your best, before you begin this shift, watch these short Great Tips videos: Initial Contact 1 and 2. These videos will give you the phrases, techniques, and strategies to make better decisions, improve the guest experience, and earn more, both in the game and on the floor. Watch now. Then play the shift.

scenes.scenario: Two people are seated at a 4-top. They are clearly waiting for 2 more to arrive.
scenes.prompt: When do you go to the table?

choices.text: Wait for the others to arrive so you don’t have to repeat yourself.
choices.feedback: You missed a Step of Service.

choices.text: Acknowledge the two with eye contact and a smile as you walk to another table.
Promptly acknowledge guests warmly with a smile and ask if they want a drink or something to nibble on while they are waiting.
choices.feedback: You performed Initial Contact at a strong level.
choices.reinforcement: Great servers never let guests feel forgotten.
choices.notebookUnlock: Perform All Steps of Service: Strong openings create trust early.

mechanic.whatYouDo: You greet promptly and offer help
mechanic.guestFeels: Guests feel noticed and cared for
mechanic.result: Trust rises, spending begins sooner, and tip potential increases.

scenes.scenario: A family sits down during a rush and starts scanning the dining room for help.
scenes.prompt: What opening line best protects the guest experience?

choices.text: I’ll be back when things slow down.
choices.feedback: The table heard that they are not the priority.

choices.text: Welcome in. I’m taking care of you tonight and I’ll get drinks started right away.
choices.feedback: You established ownership and reduced uncertainty.
choices.reinforcement: A confident opening lowers guest anxiety.
choices.notebookUnlock: Own the Table: Guests relax when they know who is caring for them.

choices.text: Do you know what you want?
choices.feedback: You skipped the welcome and made the interaction feel transactional.

scenes.scenario: Two guests say they are still waiting on friends but they have opened the drink menu.

choices.text: Offer to start drinks or a small appetizer while they wait.
choices.feedback: You created value before the full party arrived.
choices.reinforcement: Great service starts momentum without pressure.
choices.notebookUnlock: Start Spending Sooner: Early offers can improve the guest experience and the check average.

choices.text: Leave them alone until the entire party arrives.
choices.feedback: The table remained idle and unattended.

choices.text: Drop menus silently and keep walking.
choices.feedback: The action was useful, but the connection was missing.

scenes.scenario: You realize a table has waited longer than ideal before first contact.

choices.text: Avoid mentioning it and act like nothing happened.
choices.feedback: Ignoring the delay can make frustration grow.

choices.text: Apologize briefly, thank them for waiting, and immediately offer drinks.
choices.feedback: You owned the delay and moved the experience forward.
choices.notebookUnlock: Recover Fast: Guests forgive delays faster when you acknowledge and act.

choices.text: Explain that the kitchen is backed up before taking drink orders.
choices.feedback: You shifted attention to operational problems instead of guest care.

scenes.scenario: One guest is checking their phone while another keeps looking toward the host stand.
scenes.prompt: Which response best acknowledges the situation?

choices.text: Tell them their friends are late and walk away.
choices.feedback: The comment may feel judgmental and does not help the table.

choices.text: Offer water and say you can get anything started while they wait.
choices.feedback: You noticed the wait and made it easier.
choices.reinforcement: Anticipation turns waiting time into service time.

choices.text: Ask them to wave you down when everyone arrives.
choices.feedback: You put the service responsibility back on the guest.

scenes.scenario: A new table is seated while you are closing out another check. You have a short window to decide how to acknowledge them.
scenes.prompt: Choose before the timer runs out.

choices.text: Make eye contact, smile, and say you will be right with them while finishing the closeout.
choices.feedback: You acknowledged the table quickly without abandoning the active guest.
choices.reinforcement: Fast acknowledgement can be brief and still meaningful.
choices.notebookUnlock: Signal Awareness: Guests notice when you notice them.

choices.text: Finish the closeout completely before looking over.
choices.feedback: The new table was left wondering if anyone saw them.

choices.text: Interrupt the payment immediately and leave the current guest waiting.
choices.feedback: You helped one table by creating a new service problem for another.

choices.text: No decision before the table waits too long.
choices.feedback: The opportunity for prompt Initial Contact passed.
